summary: אָרַר means to pronounce a curse on someone or something. In Genesis 3 Yahweh uses the passive participle when he declares first the serpent and then the ground cursed.

senses.definition: To pronounce a curse on someone or something. The passive participle describes whoever or whatever is under the curse.

evidence.note: Yahweh says אָרוּר אַתָּה, “cursed are you,” to the serpent because of what it has done. Going on its belly and eating dust are the consequences he declares.
In אֲרוּרָה הָאֲדָמָה, “cursed is the ground,” the feminine participle agrees with the ground. Adam will eat from it in toil all his life.
